name: Sandvik AB (publ)
executive_summary: Sandvik AB is a global industrial engineering group (mining & rock solutions, machining solutions, rock processing) that the quantitative screen rates as **buy** (10/22 models, 66% composite), driven by quality-GARP signals rather than deep value. The hook is a rare Piotroski F-Score of 9/9 combined with Lynch PEG 0.43 and statutory earnings growth of 62.9%, implying the market may still be pricing cyclical normalisation rather than a structurally stronger earnings base. At P/E 26.7× and P/B 4.5× the stock is not cheap on absolute metrics, and it fails Graham, deep-value, and high-yield screens. The central debate is whether mining automation, aftermarket/service intensity, and bolt-on M&A can sustain mid-teens ROE through the cycle, or whether 2023 revenue peak (SEK 126.5bn) marks the high watermark before a prolonged industrial downturn. Primary Swedish/ESEF filings were not retrieved in this pack, limiting verification of segment mix, order backlog, and risk disclosures.
investment_thesis: For a value-oriented investor willing to accept a quality compounder rather than a net-net, Sandvik presents a coherent buy case. The screen passes five factor families—cheapness (relative), quality, dividend, GARP, and risk—with standout models including Lynch PEG, Neff PEGY (0.12), Quality Value, Economic Moat, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Piotroski F-Score, Composite Value, Earnings Quality, and Financial Health. Business quality indicators align: ROE 17.9%, operating cash flow of SEK 19.2bn (FY2025, Yahoo), and FCF of SEK 15.4bn comfortably covering dividends of SEK 7.2bn. Net debt fell from SEK 36.5bn (2022) to SEK 26.5bn (2025) while the Piotroski profile shows improving leverage, liquidity, margins, and asset turnover—all nine components passing. The stock fails traditional deep-value filters (P/B 4.5, FCF yield 3.2%, earnings yield 3.7%), so the opportunity is **growth at a reasonable price** within a franchise industrial, not a distressed rerating. Recent news flow—record Q2 2026 revenues (per earnings-call headline), multiple underground mining fleet wins, and the Diemme Filtration acquisition—supports the screen’s GARP and moat narrative, though coverage is thin and filing-backed confirmation is absent.
financial_review:
**Primary filings:** None indexed. `filings_index.json` (regime: uk_rns) lists zero filings with no annual report, half-year report, or interim release bodies available. Segment detail, management commentary, going-concern language, and contingency notes cannot be cited from regulatory extracts. The following uses **Yahoo fallback** (`financials_annual.json`).

**Income statement trend (Yahoo annual, SEK):**

| Metric | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 |
|--------|------|------|------|------|
| Revenue | 112.3bn | 126.5bn | 122.9bn | 120.7bn |
| Operating income | 19.0bn | 23.0bn | 19.2bn | 21.0bn |
| Net income | 11.2bn* | 15.3bn | 12.2bn | 14.7bn |
| Diluted EPS | 8.94 | 12.18 | 9.75 | 11.70 |
| EBITDA | 26.0bn | 29.9bn | 27.0bn | 28.7bn |

\*2022 net income includes discontinued operations (SEK 1.6bn loss).

Revenue peaked in 2023 and has softened modestly (−1.8% in 2025 vs 2024), while profitability rebounded: net income rose 20% YoY in 2025 after a 2024 trough. Gross profit held near 40% of revenue (SEK 49.0bn on SEK 120.7bn in 2025). R&D spend was SEK 4.5bn (~3.8% of sales), consistent with a technology-led positioning.

**Cash flow and capital allocation (Yahoo):** Operating cash flow strengthened from SEK 10.5bn (2022) to SEK 19.2bn (2025), though it dipped from SEK 20.6bn in 2024. Free cash flow scaled from SEK 5.9bn (2022) to SEK 15.4bn (2025), with FY2024 at SEK 15.8bn. Dividends paid rose steadily (SEK 6.0bn → 7.2bn over 2022–25). CapEx normalised to SEK 3.8bn in 2025 from SEK 5.4bn in 2023. Acquisition outflows remain material (SEK 3.0bn in 2025; SEK 15.2bn in 2022 reflects larger portfolio moves).

**Balance sheet (Yahoo, year-end 2025):** Total assets SEK 169.9bn; equity SEK 93.2bn; total debt SEK 37.1bn; net debt SEK 26.5bn; cash SEK 4.96bn. Goodwill and intangibles total SEK 62.6bn (~37% of assets). Non-current pension and post-retirement obligations SEK 3.57bn, plus defined pension benefit SEK 1.76bn. Current ratio ~1.94 (screen input). Working capital was a SEK 1.1bn OCF drag in 2025 (inventory SEK 33.2bn).

**Interim / recent quarter (Yahoo cached quarterly income, 2026):** A single 2026 quarter is present—revenue SEK 30.7bn, operating income SEK 5.33bn, net income SEK 3.88bn, diluted EPS SEK 3.09—consistent with the news headline citing “record revenues” in Q2 2026, but without a filing body this cannot be reconciled to official interim disclosures or H1/H2 splits.

**Gaps:** No annual report, interim report, or trading-update filing bodies to validate FY2025 audit opinion, segment margins, order intake/backlog, or covenant/pension footnotes. Interim analysis is limited to one Yahoo quarterly slice and news summaries.
risks_and_flags:
Without filing bodies, standard regulatory risk language (going concern, litigation reserves, covenant headroom) cannot be assessed; this is itself a research gap. From Yahoo balance-sheet data and screen metrics, several structural risks stand out:

- **Cyclicality:** Revenue has already retreated from the 2023 peak; mining and machining capex cycles can compress volumes and pricing faster than cost bases adjust.
- **Leverage and pensions:** Net debt SEK 26.5bn and total debt SEK 37.1bn remain meaningful against equity; pension-related liabilities exceed SEK 5bn combined—material though not screen-flagged.
- **Acquisition / intangibles:** Goodwill and intangibles at SEK 62.6bn create impairment and integration risk; M&A spend has been lumpy (e.g. SEK 15.2bn in 2022).
- **Valuation sensitivity:** At P/E 26.7× and EV/EBIT 23.4× (failed Acquirer’s Multiple), earnings disappointments would compress the multiple sharply; the stock fails FCF yield (3.2%) and earnings yield (3.7%) hurdles.
- **Working capital:** Rising inventory and receivable movements consumed cash in 2025; cyclical downturns could amplify this.
- **Competitive / technology:** Automation and digital mining are strategic positives but require sustained R&D; peers in mining equipment and cutting tools compete aggressively on price and service contracts.

RiskTags: cyclical, pension, leverage, competitive, accounting, other
news_highlights:
Coverage is **thin** (nine articles in `news_manifest.json`; `alternate_news.json` empty). Material items from the past year:

- **Q2 2026 results (17 Jul 2026):** “Sandvik AB (SDVKF) Q2 2026 Earnings Call Highlights: Record Revenues and Strategic Growth …” — signals strong recent top-line momentum; details not available in filing bodies.
- **M&A (23 Jun 2026):** “Sandvik agrees to acquire Italy’s Diemme Filtration” — Diemme to form a Filtration division within Rock Processing; expands processing/filtration exposure.
- **Order wins (Jun–Aug 2026):** Multiple underground mining fleet contracts—Barminco/Bellevue Gold (15 Jun), CoMinVi (6 Jul), Viscaria copper mine automation (6 Aug), Karowe mine fleet (14 Aug)—support mining solutions demand and aftermarket/service model.
- **Sentiment (26 Jun 2026):** Zacks upgrade to Buy on earnings optimism; sector outperformance pieces (14 Jul, 26 Jun) are comparative, not fundamental.

No material governance, regulatory enforcement, or management-change headlines in the manifest. Strategy emphasis from news: automation, on-site service organisations, and bolt-on filtration M&A.
research_rationale: Yahoo-backed financials and a perfect Piotroski score support the screen’s quality-GARP buy case, but absent primary filings and with revenue still below the 2023 peak, conviction is moderated pending Swedish annual/interim verification.
